choice.psg: ❶ One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. ❷ For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. ❸ Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. ❹ What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. ❺ It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. ❻ The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. ❼ To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. ❽ First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. ❾ Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. ❿ Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. ⓫ Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. ⓬ Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. ⓭ Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. ⓮ This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

read.ko: 우리는 세계 경제 속에 살고 있으며, 프랑스 시장에서 기기를 판매하고 싶은 모든 회사는 그들의 제품에 수리 가능성 지수에 따라 라벨을 붙여야 할 것이다.

read.en: ⓫ If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.
read.ko: 만약 이 지수가 성공적이라면, 우리는 전 세계의 더 많은 나라들이 프랑스의 혁신적인 선례를 따르는 것을 보길 기대할 수 있다.

read.en: ❶ When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves.
read.ko: 소비자들에게 유용한 조언과 함께 알맞은 도구와 재료가 주어지면, 그들은 전자 제품에 발생하는 대부분의 손상을 직접 수리할 수 있다.

read.en: ❷ That is why Repair Cafés were started.
read.ko: 그것이 수리 카페가 시작된 이유이다.

read.en: ❸ They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices.
read.ko: 그곳은 사람들이 함께 모여 자신들의 고장 난 장치들을 고칠 수 있는 자유로운 만남의 장소이다.

read.en: ❹ The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.
read.ko: 그 카페들은 기술적인 조언을 줄 수 있고, 사람들에게 물건을 고치는 방법을 가르쳐 줄 수 있는 자원봉사자 전문가들을 직원으로 두고 있다.

read.en: ❺ The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009.
read.ko: 가장 첫 번째 수리 카페는 네덜란드의 도시 암스테르담에서 2009년에 열렸다.

read.en: ❻ It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries.
read.ko: 그것은 너무 성공적이어서 그 아이디어가 곧 이웃 나라들로 확산되었다.

read.en: ❼ Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world.
read.ko: 얼마 후, 전 세계 30개국 이상에 수리 카페가 생겼다.

read.en: ❽ Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics.
read.ko: 고장 난 물건들이 전자 쓰레기가 되는 것을 막는 것과 더불어, 이 카페들은 또한 사람들이 전자 제품의 수리와 보수 관리에 대한 매우 유용한 기술들과 지식을 공 유할 수 있도록 장려한다.

read.en: ❾ They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.
read.ko: 점점 더 많은 사람들이 자원봉사를 하기 위해 신청하면서, 이 카페들은 계속해서 인기를 얻고 있다.

read.en: ❿ By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans.
read.ko: 사람들이 배울 수 있는 공간을 제공함으로써, 수리 카페들은 개인이 자신들의 장치를 유지하고 그것들의 수명을 연장할 수 있게 한다.

read.en: ⓫ Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
read.ko: 게다가 그것들은 우리의 미래에 막대한 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있는 지속 가능한 관점을 조성한다.

read.en: ⓬ Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop?
read.ko: 노트북을 떨어뜨렸던 소녀 Liz를 기억하는가?

read.en: ⓭ Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life.
read.ko: 그녀가 손상된 장치와 기기를 수리하는 것이 그저 일상의 한 부분인 세상에 살고 있었다고 상상해 보라.

read.en: ⓮ If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one.
read.ko: 만약 그랬다면, 그녀의 선택지는 비싼 수리를 위해 비용을 지불하거나 노트북을 버리고 새것을 사는 것으로 제한되지는 않았을 것이다.

read.en: ⓯ She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself.
read.ko: 그녀는 인터넷에서 필요한 부품들을 주문하고, 그것들을 직접 교체할 수 있었을 것이다.

read.en: ⓰ Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it.
read.ko: 그렇지 않으면, 그녀는 그것을 고치는 방법에 대한 조언을 얻기 위해 고장 난 장치를 가장 가까운 수리 카페에 가지고 갈 수도 있었을 것이다.

read.en: ⓱ Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score.
read.ko: 그녀는 높은 수리 가능성 점수를 가진 노트북을 구매했을 것이기 때문에, 그것을 수리하는 것은 아마 아주 어렵지는 않았을 것이다.

read.en: ⓲ In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together.
read.ko: 사실, 이 지속 가능한 세상은 우리가 그것을 향해 함께 노력한다면 우리 모두가 누릴 수 있는 미래이다.

read.en: ⓳ Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
read.ko: 훨씬 더 중요한 것은 그것은 사람들이 훨씬 적은 전자 쓰레기를 발생시킬 미래이며, 이는 우리의 지구를 모두를 위한 더 깨끗하고 건강한 곳으로 만들 것이라는 것이다.

para.en: ❶ On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. ❷ Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. ❸ She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. ❹ Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. ❺ Besides, the laptop is about five years old. ❻ In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. ❼ In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. ❽ If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. ❾ What exactly is e-waste? ❿ The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. ⓫ Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. ⓬ To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. ⓭ In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. ⓮ Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. ⓯ For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. ⓰ Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.

❶ One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. ❷ For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. ❸ Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. ❹ What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. ❺ It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. ❻ The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. ❼ To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. ❽ First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. ❾ Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. ❿ Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. ⓫ Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. ⓬ Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. ⓭ Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. ⓮ This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause.

❶ In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. ❷ Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. ❸ The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. ❹ A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. ❺ The index was designed to have two positive effects. ❻ Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. ❼ Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. ❽ As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. ❾ The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. ❿ We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. ⓫ If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.

❶ When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. ❷ That is why Repair Cafés were started. ❸ They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. ❹ The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. ❺ The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. ❻ It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. ❼ Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. ❽ Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. ❾ They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. ❿ By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. ⓫ Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future. ⓬ Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? ⓭ Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. ⓮ If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. ⓯ She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. ⓰ Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. ⓱ Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, as she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. ⓲ In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. ⓳ Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
